questions.q: What does Oster recommend instead of one-size-fits-all parenting advice?
a: A personal framework built from costs and benefits
Following the most popular parenting book
Trusting your pediatrician without question
Copying what worked for your own parents
questions.why: Lesson 1 says there is no single right answer, so parents should weigh the costs and benefits of their own situation.

questions.q: In the nanny versus daycare example, what does the summary say?
a: The better choice depends on your income and priorities
Daycare is always the healthier option
A nanny is always worth the extra cost
Neither option affects a child's development
questions.why: The summary lists money, personalized care and social contact as inputs whose weight varies by family.

questions.q: Why might the breastfeeding IQ studies be misleading?
a: Educated, wealthier mothers are more likely to breastfeed
Breastfed children are rarely tested for IQ
The studies included too few children to matter
Formula companies funded most of the research
questions.why: Lesson 3 calls socioeconomic background a confounding variable, and the IQ gap shrinks once it is controlled.

questions.q: Which studies does Oster consider the most reliable?
a: Large randomized controlled trials
Small observational studies
Personal stories from other parents
Studies that compare different countries
questions.why: The summary says randomization and large samples best control for confounding variables.
